title: Aquatic Momentum Lab: Mug & Fish Collisions
description: A top-down physics sandbox where the user launches a coffee mug and a fish across a frictionless table to study conservation of momentum and energy. Users configure mass, velocity vectors, and restitution for each object, trigger collisions, and use undo/redo to iterate on parameters while observing real-time momentum and kinetic energy readouts.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load coffeeMug.glb and BarramundiFish.glb and place them on a large flat plane representing a frictionless air-hockey-style table with a subtle grid texture. Camera starts at an elevated 45-degree angle; OrbitControls allow rotation and zoom. Add ambient light (0.4) and two directional lights for clear shadows. Physics: Implement a simple 2D momentum-based collision system on the XZ plane. Each object has configurable mass (slider 0.5-10 kg) and initial velocity vector (two sliders for Vx and Vz, range -10 to 10 m/s). Add a restitution slider (0-1) that couples both objects, controlling elastic vs inelastic behavior. Display a HUD panel showing each object's current momentum (p=mv), total system momentum, total kinetic energy, and a conservation-violation indicator that flags if totals drift. Interactions (10-14 steps): 1) Adjust mug mass, 2) set mug Vx, 3) set mug Vz, 4) adjust fish mass, 5) set fish Vx, 6) set fish Vz, 7) set shared restitution, 8) press Launch to animate both objects gliding toward each other, 9) observe collision resolution with objects bouncing/sticking based on restitution, 10) press Pause to freeze mid-simulation, 11) use Undo button to revert last parameter change and re-simulate, 12) use Redo to restore it, 13) toggle a momentum-vector arrow overlay on each object, 14) press Reset to return objects to start positions. During simulation, animate objects smoothly with requestAnimationFrame; on collision detect via bounding-sphere overlap, compute post-collision velocities using 1D elastic/inelastic formulas projected onto the collision normal. The mug should rotate slightly on impact; the fish should wobble with a subtle tail oscillation. Keep all code in one file under 500 lines.
